The Shinigami Selvedge is an 18oz Japanese selvedge denim made from 100% cotton with black rope-dyed yarns. A slubby texture combined with deep black tones gives the fabric its heavy, imposing presence and pronounced surface character.
The fabric takes its name from the Shinigami, figures from Japanese folklore often described as spirits or gods associated with death and the passage between worlds. p-nakedandfamousdenim-14984426258797.d:
Prince of Slub is a 23oz Japanese selvedge denim that continues the lineage of Naked & Famous’ most aggressively textured fabrics, following in the footsteps of King of Slub and Emperor of Slub.
Like its predecessors, Prince of Slub uses extremely slubby warp yarns that are heavyweight, irregular, and rich in surface variation, but introduces a newly developed weft to give this edition its own identity within the Slub series.
Where King of Slub pushed texture through custom-developed uneven yarns and Emperor of Slub amplified that effect through slow, low-tension weaving, Prince of Slub refines the balance. The result is a denim with intense tactile depth, pronounced peaks and valleys, and irregularities that catch light, emphasize wear patterns, and reward time spent fading it.
The fabric is left unsanforized and loomstate, meaning it remains exactly as it was after weaving, without pre-shrinking or finishing to compress the yarns. This preserves the raw slub character and allows the denim to shrink with washing and evolve dramatically with wear, delivering the transformation that defines the Slub series.

The “Big Buck” is a unique collaboration with Simmons Bilt in Scotland, based on our traditional Western shirt silhouette and handmade from European deerskin. The leather used comes from deer living in the hills and mountains of Germany and Austria. As these are wild animals, many hides display natural scars — a byproduct of antlered males fighting during the rutting season.
The tanning method is an old and traditional process known as Sämischgerbung, a chemical-free technique that, while time-consuming, produces an incredibly soft yet hard-wearing leather. We source this leather from Kolesch Tannery (https://www.gerberei-kolesch.de/) — the oldest working tannery in Germany — where it is both tanned and hand-dyed.
This tanning process results in a beige-coloured leather, visible on the inside of the shirt. To achieve the final colour, a natural dye is applied by hand. Because the dye is brushed onto the surface rather than dip-dyed, subtle variations in the finish can occur, depending on how each hide absorbs the pigment. From the initial tanning process to the finished leather, production takes a full year.
